To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cholesterol-lowering action of colchicine is due to the fact that it increases the biosynthesis of prostaglandin PGE1 and that this action is due to the colchicine-induced formation of a new metabolite which has a structure closely related to that of melatonin, the hormone of darkness.

(a) PGE1 is a critical substance that inhibits cholesterol and collagen biosyntheses, inhibits platelet aggregation and smooth muscle proliferation and dilates vessels, (b) cholesterol biosynthesis, platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction are enhanced by TXA2 and inhibited by PGE1 and (c) PGE1 biosyntheses are inhibited by cholesterol and stimulated by essential fatty acids and TXA2.

the essential fatty acids, linoleic and arachidonic acid, are necessary for normal cardiovascular function, that cholesterol biosynthesis is controlled by the balance of PGE1 and TXA2 in the vascular system and that the balance of PEG1 and TXA 2 is controlled by the essential fatty acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cholesterol, essential fatty acid and prostaglandin metabolism in the development of cardiovascular disease and the possible role of melatonin in the prevention of cardiovascular disease.
the development of a unifying concept which can be tested in the laboratory.
the development of a new approach to the treatment and prevention of cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of cardiovascular disorders is determined by the relative rates of cholesterol and PGE1 biosyntheses.

cholesterol biosynthesis is a necessary and sufficient cause of cardiovascular disease and that the essential fatty acids are the primary regulators of cholesterol biosynthesis, but that the effects of essential fatty acids and cholesterol are mediated by the prostaglandins.

the essential fatty acids and cholesterol are not the causes of cardiovascular disease, but are involved in a complex feedback system which is the basis for the development of cardiovascular disease and its prevention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway is not the only pathway for cholesterol biosynthesis and that cholesterol biosynthesis is not the only way to produce cholesterol.

the essential fatty acids, linoleic, arachidonic and gamma-linolenic acids, have a major role in preventing cardiovascular disease by increasing PGE1 levels, and that the effects of other factors are mediated through their effects on PGE1 biosynthesi.

the hypothesis predicts the existence of a negative feedback control mechanism which regulates the balance of PGE1 and TXA2, which in turn controls the balance of cholesterol, essential fatty acid, collagen and melatonin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway is not a simple linear pathway, but a complex system of interrelated feedback loops.
cholesterol is not the only risk factor for atherosclerosis.
the use of cholesterol-lowering agents should be accompanied by the use of agents which enhance PGE1 biosynthetic activity.
